A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 56-page versions of the same STABLEEDIT study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, algorithm, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original model-editing experiments, baseline comparisons, scalability measurements, ablations, and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix B, including editing performance, general-capability tests, and mechanism diagnostics.

M1.justification: STABLEEDIT retains the same warm-up stage, running-statistics updates, full covariance whitening, and ridge-regression updates. Algorithm 1 is unchanged; the matrix-label correction in Section 3.3 does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ZsRE, FEVER, WikiBigEdit, ULTRAEDITBENCH, MedCF, and five GLUE tasks. The warm-up mismatch and abrupt distribution-shift scenarios were already present in v1.

E2.justification: FT, MEMIT, ALPHAEDIT, MEND, MALMEN, RLEDIT, and ULTRAEDIT retain their participation in the corresponding comparisons. Updating ULTRAEDIT's citation from Gu et al. (2026) to Gu et al. (2025) does not introduce a different comparator.

E3.justification: Model configurations, edit budgets, batch sizes, metrics, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 merely reformats the same MedCF split counts; the new metric-reliability discussion does not change the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablations, warm-up size and placement tests, distribution-mismatch tests, statistics-only warm-up, update-geometry diagnostics, drift analyses, and hidden-state-scaling ablation are retained. No supplementary experiment or analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including the 0.95 confidence intervals described for the representation visualizations. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–15 and Figures 1–14 retain their numerical results and plotted findings. Section 5.4 now calls the 0.43-point warm-up statistic an average absolute change, but v1 already described it that way in Appendix B.6.1.

T1.justification: Remark D.9 removes the assertion that Theorem 3.8(b) establishes a uniform lower bound as well as upper bounds on the instance-specific update norm. This is a limited correction to the stated mathematical guarantee; the assumptions, theorem statements, equations, and proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: explaining LN's positive cumulative effect and stability mechanism, deriving STABLEEDIT, and demonstrating competitive performance on long editing sequences.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a specific qualification that token-matching metrics may not fully capture genuine editing effects, identifying evaluation reliability as a future direction. Remark D.9 also narrows its description of the norm guarantee, although its non-vanishing interpretation remains.

D1.justification: The code-access link, NVIDIA A6000 hardware disclosure, learning rates, ridge parameter, warm-up sizes, editable-layer settings, and runtime accounting are retained. Reformatting learning-rate notation does not disclose different settings.

R1.justification: The new evaluation caveat cites Yang et al. (2025), The mirage of model editing, and Gu et al. (2026), The model agreed, but didn't learn. These are limited additions concerning evaluation reliability; the central positioning relative to prior editors is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammar and terminology edits, updates affiliations and publication information, revises bibliographic metadata, and inserts a short evaluation-reliability paragraph. The narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is enlarged and moved from the left to the right column on page 8. Publication information and text additions cause local reflow and page-break changes. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The new Appendix A.1 caveat better qualifies the empirical evidence, and Remark D.9 removes an unsupported lower-bound assertion. These provide modest gains in accuracy and transparency. The correction remains incomplete because the remark still claims updates are 'neither vanishing nor exploding'; the underlying experiments and proofs are unchanged.
